scam.title: What is a scam exchanger?
scam.text:
A scam exchanger is a website or service that pretends to be a legitimate crypto exchange but is actually built to steal funds. Such platforms may use fake rates, fake reviews or copy the design of well-known services.

They can disappear right after receiving your money or stall until it is too late to get it back. Remember: a good-looking website is no guarantee of honesty.

detect.title: How to spot a scammer?
detect.text:
1. Check the domain and website address — scammers often use lookalike names.
2. Read reviews on independent platforms, not only on the exchanger's own website.
3. Look at the service's history — a brand new site with no reputation is a risk.

Our goal is to help you recognise and avoid dishonest exchangers.

avoid.title: How to avoid getting scammed?
avoid.text:
1. Never transfer money directly to strangers' personal cards.
2. Use only verified services from trusted listings.
3. Compare the exchanger's data with information on well-known monitorings.

We collect and update this data so you can exchange crypto safely.

victim.title: What to do if you became a victim?
victim.text:
If you suspect you have been scammed:

1. Collect all the evidence right away (screenshots, chat logs, receipts).
2. Contact your bank's support and try to reverse the transfer.
3. File a complaint with the cyber police and warn other users through MoneySwap support.

We do everything we can to make such cases rarer and keep users protected.
